subject: Recap: Novacare discovery — throughput / SLOs / routing next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: James Carter <j.carter@novacare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: Novacare discovery — throughput / SLOs / routing next steps

James — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Call highlights (from Novacare):
- Primary pain: current provider has intermittent latency spikes (P95 often > 450ms) under peak hours causing UI timeouts for clinical users.
- Target SLOs: P50 < 80ms, P95 < 200ms for short text generations (prompt windows typically 128–256 tokens).
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~120 requests/sec for the triage assistant; peak bursts up to ~600 rps for batch processing windows.
- Models under consideration: 13B & 70B family (they prefer an open model) — accuracy trade-offs matter for medical summarization.
- Deployment constraints: private VPC deployment (HIPAA adjacency), strict audit logs, 90-day retention for transcripts.

Proposed technical approach (Redwood):
- Start with a dedicated private deployment (sandbox VPC) to benchmark 13B quantized and 70B int8.
- Use continuous batching with a max latency floor of 180ms for P95; implement prefix/KV caching for common prompts.
- Smart routing policy: route low-latency interactive traffic to smaller model variant; heavy summarization/batch to larger model with relaxed latency SLO.
- Monitoring: we’ll provide token-level latency breakdown and an initial SLO matrix (attached).

Action items / next steps:
1) Novacare to provide a representative prompt set (10–20 prompts) + throughput sketch for peak windows by EOD Thu.
2) Redwood to stand up a sandbox dedicated pool and run a 3-day benchmark (13B int4 and 70B int8) — propose kickoff Mon 2027-04-18.
3) Legal/procurement: Novacare to share baseline contract questions; Redwood to pull SOC2 artifacts for review.

Attachments: novacare_mpa_v1.xlsx (mutual-action plan draft), slo_matrix_20270411.csv (initial SLO targets and measurement points).

If that matches your read, we’ll schedule the sandbox kickoff and put Marissa on the bench build.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

---
Redwood Inference — production-first inference for LLMs.
From: James Carter <j.carter@novacare.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Novacare discovery — throughput / SLOs / routing next steps

Rachel — thanks for the clear recap, that aligns well. A few clarifications from our side:
- The 120 rps steady-state is for the triage path; another async summarization pipeline handles bulk jobs during off-peak and will need to sustain ~800 rps for short windows (10–15 minutes).
- Prompt set: we have a redacted set of 25 prompts and a 1-week anonymized traffic sample — I’ll attach to the MPA in the shared Drive by Thursday.
- Model preference: we’d like to evaluate the 13B first for latency, but need a quality baseline vs a 70B family model for edge-case clinical accuracy.

One ask on compliance: can Redwood provide an export of audit logs (read/write events) and evidence of KMS integration during the sandbox? Our security team needs to validate before pilot access.

Happy to run the kickoff on 4/18 — James

James Carter
Director, Product Engineering — Novacare
j.carter@novacare.com | +1 (646) 555-0199
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: James Carter <j.carter@novacare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Novacare discovery — throughput / SLOs / routing next steps

Thanks James — that helps. Two quick notes:
- We can export per-request audit logs and provide a trimmed sample during the sandbox. KMS integration is available for the private package; I’ll include our integration guide in the Drive link.
- For the benchmark, we’ll run: 1) 13B int4 with aggressive batching to hit latency targets, 2) 70B int8 with larger batch sizing for throughput runs. We’ll capture P50/P90/P95 and token-level CPU/GPU breakdowns.

I’ve scheduled a 60-min kickoff for Mon 2027-04-18 10:00–11:00 PT (invitation sent). Agenda: onboarding, data handoff steps, measurement plan, success criteria for the 3-day benchmark.

Internal owners: Marissa — you’ll lead bench infra and results analysis. Sean — can you prepare the SLO measurement dashboard template (token-level breakdown + alert thresholds)? I attached an initial SLO matrix for quick reference.

Marissa / Sean — please confirm owners and any blockers.

Rachel

Attachments: slo_matrix_20270411.csv
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-13T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Recap: Novacare discovery — bench owners & checklist

Marissa / Sean — forwarding the thread and pulling out the internal checklist so we have a single source of truth: 
- Marissa: stand up a sandbox dedicated pool (4 GPUs, T4-like profile) with VPC peering and KMS enabled. Deploy both 13B int4 and 70B int8 images.
- Sean: build the SLO dashboard template and create alert definitions for P95 > 200ms and error-rate > 1%. Include token-level cost estimates per model.
- Both: prepare an artifacts bundle for Novacare security: sample audit logs, KMS integration docs, and a short runbook for data deletion after the sandbox.

Timeline: kickoff 4/18 — bench ready by 4/18 EOD, 3-day run 4/19–4/21, deliverables: latency/throughput report, quality delta notes, recommended routing policy.

I’ll update the HubSpot deal with owners and timeline.

Thanks — Rachel
